title: Review: Magnetic fields and field patterns; Magnetic materials, domains and permeability; Fields of currents (quantitative); Force on moving charges; Biot–Savart law and Ampère's law
qualification: AP Physics C: Electricity and Magnetism
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics C: Electricity and Magnetism (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: NEW-magnetic-materials-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; MG03-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; MG03-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; NEW-magnetic-materials-1#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: MG03-1#N.16, MG04-1#N.12b, NEW-magnetic-materials-1#N.10b, MG03-1#N.17, MG04-1#N.13, NEW-magnetic-materials-1#N.11, MG04-1#N.14.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Domain
items.clue: Small region of iron in which the atomic dipoles line up with those next to them.

items.label: Kinetic energy
items.clue: Quantity of a moving charge that a magnetic push leaves unchanged, like its speed.

items.label: Work
items.clue: Never done by the magnetic push on a moving charge, as it acts at 90° to the velocity.

items.label: Permeability
items.clue: Symbol μ: how strongly the dipoles of a substance align in response to an external field.

questions.stem: A particle of mass m and charge q > 0 enters a region of uniform magnetic field of magnitude B with speed v. Its velocity has a component v∥ parallel to the field and a component v⊥ perpendicular to the field, and it moves along a helix. What distance does the particle move along the field direction during one revolution?

options.text: 2πmv/(qB)
mv⊥/(qB)
2πmv∥v⊥/(qB)
2πmv∥/(qB)

questions.stem: Two long straight parallel wires are 0.040 m apart. Wire 1 carries a current of 12 A, and wire 2 carries a current of 8.0 A in the opposite direction. What is the magnitude of the magnetic force exerted by wire 1 on a 1.5 m length of wire 2? (Use μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A.)
At room temperature and in a weak external field, which ranking of the magnetic permeabilities of iron (μ_Fe), aluminum (μ_Al), copper (μ_Cu) and free space (μ₀) is correct?

options.text: μ_Fe > μ_Al = μ₀ = μ_Cu
μ_Fe > μ_Al > μ₀ > μ_Cu
μ_Fe > μ_Cu > μ₀ > μ_Al
μ_Cu > μ_Al > μ_Fe > μ₀

questions.stem: Two protons enter two separate regions at the same speed. Region 1 contains only a uniform electric field; region 2 contains only a uniform magnetic field. Each proton enters at right angles to the field lines. Gravity is negligible. A short time later, which statement is correct?

options.text: Both protons still have their starting speed, because each force began at right angles to the motion.
Only the proton in the magnetic field still has its starting speed.
Only the proton in the electric field still has its starting speed.
Both protons have sped up, because each one is pushed by a force.

questions.stem: Two long straight parallel wires, X and Y, are 5.0 cm apart in air. X carries 2.0 A and Y carries 6.0 A, in the same direction. What is the magnetic force on a 1.0 m length of each wire?

options.text: 4.8 × 10⁻⁵ N on X; 1.4 × 10⁻⁴ N on Y
4.8 × 10⁻⁵ N on each, towards the other wire
1.6 × 10⁻⁵ N on X; 4.8 × 10⁻⁵ N on Y
4.8 × 10⁻⁵ N on each, away from the other wire

questions.explanation: Field of X at Y: 2 × 10⁻⁷ × 2.0 ÷ 0.050 = 8.0 × 10⁻⁶ T. Force on 1.0 m of Y: 8.0 × 10⁻⁶ × 6.0 × 1.0 = 4.8 × 10⁻⁵ N. Newton's third law: the force on X is the same size, and same-direction currents attract.

questions.stem: Rods of nickel, aluminum and copper, identical in size and shape, are each placed in turn in a strong external magnetic field and then removed from it. Which of the rods can then be a permanent magnet?

options.text: The nickel and aluminum rods, which were both attracted
All three rods, since all three of them are metals
None of them, as their dipoles return to random directions
The nickel rod alone, as its domains can stay aligned

questions.stem: A light, loosely wound coil of wire, like a soft spring, hangs vertically. A large steady current is passed through it. What happens to the length of the coil?

options.text: It gets shorter: neighbouring turns carry current the same way, so they attract.
It gets longer, because neighbouring turns carry like currents, and like currents repel.
It stays the same, because the coil's own field cannot exert a force on the coil itself.
It gets longer, because the field inside the coil pushes the turns apart along its axis.

questions.explanation: Each turn is like a parallel wire beside the next, with current the same way: they pull together and the coil contracts.
